items.prompt: The interviewer says: 200 M daily users, each sends 40 messages a day, kept forever. You're about to choose the message store.
items.why: Concrete volumes before a storage decision → turn them into writes/s and TB/year first. The store choice depends on those numbers.

items.prompt: Product asks for 'p99 checkout latency under 300 ms and 99.95% availability' and wants to know what that allows per dependency.
items.why: Percentile targets, nines and latency budgets along a call path are the latency/throughput/availability topic, not load sizing.

items.prompt: Your estimate shows about 20 Gbps of outbound image traffic, mostly the same popular images.
items.why: Huge static egress repeated across users → push it to the edge with a CDN. Adding servers or shards would just move the bandwidth bill.

items.prompt: Your estimate: 150 000 writes/s sustained and 400 TB of rows after a year.
items.why: Sustained writes and size beyond one node → partition the data. Caches and replicas don't add write capacity.

items.prompt: DAU is 8 M, each user views 300 items a day and edits about 1 a day; the team wants to know whether a cache is worth adding.
items.why: Nobody has turned the numbers into a read/write ratio and QPS yet (≈ 28k reads/s vs ≈ 90 writes/s). Estimate first, and the caching decision follows from it.

items.prompt: The interview just started with 'design a ride-sharing app' and you're unsure which features matter.
items.why: Before any numbers you need scope: functional and non-functional requirements. That's step one of the framework, and estimates come after.

items.prompt: You must decide whether a user's last 1 000 notifications for all 50 M users fit in memory on a few cache nodes.
items.why: 'Does it fit?' is a sizing question: 50 M × 1 000 × ~200 B ≈ 10 TB, which settles it before you pick a tool.
